methodologyMarkdown:
## Overview
The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) publishes meeting documents, decisions, lists and code-of-conduct materials at https://www.cbd.int/documents. The site is a traditional server-rendered Drupal-style catalog, not a JS SPA, so a plain HTTP GET returns real anchor tags with document hrefs that can be scraped directly.

## Search
There is no JSON/REST search API. A server-side search form exists with facets (Subject, Country, Year 1988-2027, Month, Title keyword). The documented search URL https://www.cbd.int/documents?search={query} loads a server-rendered results page; more advanced filtering is form-driven. Simple keyword search via the query parameter is the reliable entry point.

## Filters
The HTML form exposes Subject, Country, Year and Month facets, but these are not cleanly reflected as stable URL query parameters in the catalog view, so no filterSchema is declared. Year/subject filtering would require replicating the form POST.

## Download
Documents appear as direct .pdf links (paths under /doc/, e.g. /doc/meetings/...pdf, /doc/lists/events-scbd.pdf). Downloading is a straightforward GET of the resolved absolute URL. Multilingual variants (ar/en/es/fr/ru/zh) are common and encoded in the filename.

## Metadata & Enrichment
No per-document metadata endpoint. Title and language come from anchor text and filename suffix. No enrichment adapter is warranted.

## Limitations
Server-rendered and scrapable, but the search/facet system is form-based rather than a clean parameterized API, limiting programmatic filtering. Multilingual duplicates require de-duplication by base filename.
probeNotes: WebFetch of https://www.cbd.int/documents?search=biodiversity returned server-rendered HTML with real .pdf anchor hrefs (/doc/meetings/*.pdf, /doc/lists/events-scbd.pdf) and a search form with Subject/Country/Year/Month facets. No JS-only shell, no repository API found.
